note: Ground truth built by agents reading the repo only; TokenHack's router and index were off-limits during construction.

queries.question: What decides whether the shield icon next to the URL is shown plain, with a dot, or as an alert?
queries.why: PrivacyIconLogic.privacyIcon(for: PrivacyInfo) at lines 34-48 returns .daxLogo for DDG search, .alert when malicousSiteThreatKind != .none, and .shieldWithDot when !https || isUserUnprotected(domain:) || invalid server trust; the simpler privacyIcon(for: URL?) overload is at lines 26-32.

queries.question: Where does the app handle moving between foreground and background, and what happens if an unexpected lifecycle event arrives?
queries.why: AppStateTransitions.swift lines 23-113 defines apply(event:) for Initializing/Launching/Foreground/Background/Terminating, and lines 122-132 define handleUnexpectedEvent which logs and fires the .appDidTransitionToUnexpectedState daily pixel. AppStateMachine.swift lines 22-69 declares AppEvent/AppAction/AppState and the AppStateMachine that drives currentState = currentState.apply(event:).

queries.question: If a user turns on clearing tabs and data after inactivity, where is the delay actually checked?
queries.why: AutoClear.shouldClearData(elapsedTime:) at lines 73-92 switches on settings.timing (.termination, .delay5min/15/30/60) comparing elapsedTime against 5/15/30/60 minutes; clearDataIfEnabledAndTimeExpired at lines 94-104 compares against the timestamp set by startClearingTimer (lines 69-71). Note the UI-test override at line 76-78 that shortens it to 5 seconds.

queries.question: Why do the top and bottom UI strips slide out of the way when you scroll a web page, and what makes them come back?
queries.why: BarsAnimator holds the revealed/transitioning/hidden state machine: revealedAndScrolling (lines 70-87), transitioningAndScrolling (89-122, including the iOS 18 PDF debounce workaround), hiddenAndScrolling with the bottom-bounce reveal gesture (124-145), calculateTransitionRatio (147-160) and didFinishScrolling's >0.5 snap decision (162-195). BrowserChromeManager is the UIScrollViewDelegate that feeds it, with canHideBars(for:) at lines 145-148 refusing to hide when the content is shorter than the viewport.

queries.question: How long can someone keep viewing their saved logins before we make them prove who they are again?
queries.why: UserSession.swift lines 22-49: Constants.defaultTimeout = 15 seconds, and isSessionValid (lines 35-40) requires timeInterval > 0 (explicitly to stop users winding the device clock back) and < sessionTimeout. AutofillLoginSession.swift lines 23-40 subclasses it and gates lastAccessedAccount on isSessionValid; callers such as AutofillLoginListViewModel and AutofillLoginPromptViewController read isSessionValid to skip re-auth.

queries.question: When browsing data gets wiped, which sites keep their cookies and local storage, and where is that exception list kept?
queries.why: Fireproofing.swift lines 37-84: UserDefaultsFireproofing stores allowedDomains in a UserDefaults wrapper and always appends the DDG host plus SubscriptionCookieManager.cookieDomain (lines 57-62); isAllowed(cookieDomain:)/isAllowed(fireproofDomain:) are the membership checks. WebCacheManager.swift lines 169-210 does the actual wipe: clearDataForSafelyRemovableDataTypes, then clearFireproofableDataForNonFireproofDomains and clearCookiesForNonFireproofedDomains filter records/cookies through fireproofing.isAllowed; the fireproofable set (cookies, localStorage, IndexedDB) is defined at lines 66-78.

queries.question: When you start typing in the search field, how are your saved bookmarks ordered so the most likely one shows first?
queries.why: The private score(_:_:_:) at lines 207-254 builds the ranking: favourites start at 0 and non-favourites at -1, +200 for a title matching the whole query from its leading boundary, +100 for a mid-string word match, +10 for matching every whitespace token, +300 when the domain starts with the first token, +50 when the title does. score(query:input:) (189-205) drops anything <= 0 and search(query:) (256-268) sorts descending by score.

queries.question: If someone clicks through the big red phishing warning and loads the site anyway, how do we remember not to block them again?
queries.why: MaliciousSiteProtectionNavigationHandler keeps maliciousURLExemptions: [URL: ThreatKind] and bypassedMaliciousSiteThreatKind (lines 64-66). visitSite(url:errorData:) at lines 146-155 records the exemption; handleMaliciousExemptions (167-173) re-reads it on each navigation and shouldBypassMaliciousSiteProtection (175-178) short-circuits detection when a bypass is active or the URL is DDG-owned. purgeMaliciousDectionTasksIfNeeded (180-191) clears pending detection tasks on a new main-frame navigation.

queries.question: A tab's web view gets thrown away under memory pressure — how do we bring back its scroll position and half-filled forms when the user returns to it?
queries.why: TabInteractionStateDiskSource.swift lines 35-142: state blobs are written per-tab into Caches/<bundleId>/webview-interaction/<tab.uid> with .atomic + .completeFileProtectionUntilFirstUserAuthentication (saveState, 69-93); popLastStateForTab (95-108) reads and immediately deletes; removeAll(excluding:) (116-128) garbage-collects files for closed tabs. TabViewController.swift calls saveState on viewWillDisappear (line 482) and onApplicationWillResignActive (line 572), and attachWebView feeds the blob into restoreInteractionStateToWebView (line 632, implementation around line 3214).

queries.question: If a usage-stat request fails because the phone was offline, do we ever try again, and how long do we hold onto it?
queries.why: PersistentPixel.fire(...) at lines 91-125 stamps PixelParameters.originalPixelTimestamp and, on failure, appends a PersistentPixelMetadata to storage. sendQueuedPixels (198-234) rate-limits reprocessing to Constants.minimumProcessingInterval (1 hour in release, 1 minute in DEBUG, lines 47-51). The private fire(queuedPixels:) at lines 239-289 drops anything whose stored timestamp is older than date28DaysAgo (line 245, checked at 248-254), tags retries with PixelParameters.retriedPixel = "1" (line 266), and only removes IDs that resend successfully.

queries.question: How can we tell that someone deleted the app and installed it again rather than being a genuinely first-time user?
queries.why: KeychainReturnUserMeasurement at lines 35-123: isReturningUser (47-49) is just hasAnyKeychainItems(), which queries kSecClassGenericPassword and kSecClassKey with kSecMatchLimitOne (99-121) — keychain entries survive app deletion, so their presence means a prior install. writeSecureATB (61-90) stores the ATB under "returning-user-atb" with kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked and synchronizable:false. DefaultVariantManager.selectVariant consumes this to force the "ru" variant.

queries.question: The server rejects a sync upload with a 413 or a 429 — where do we turn that into the message the user sees, and how do we stop nagging them repeatedly?
queries.why: handleSyncError(_:modelType:) at lines 189-227 maps status codes to error types: 409 -> count limit exceeded, 413 -> request size limit exceeded, 400 -> bad request, 401 -> invalidLoginCredentials, 418/429 -> tooManyRequests, each per bookmarks/credentials/settings. syncIsPaused (229-261) sets the isSyncBookmarksPaused / isSyncCredentialsPaused / isSyncPaused flags and fires daily pixels. showSyncPausedAlertIfNeeded (262-289) guards on didShow* flags so each alert appears once, and for the non-actionable tooManyRequests case defers to shouldShowAlertForNonActionableError (144-163), which needs 10 consecutive errors or no successful sync in 12h, plus 24h since the last notification.
